<!-- plain-summary -->
This is about proving that Wyrd's production metadata database actually behaves correctly on real hardware under real trouble — network partitions, clock skew, process pauses, and genuine disk I/O — not just in the simulator. It matters because the failure simulator can only test Wyrd's model of the store; this work confirms the real database matches that model, and every surprise it uncovers is turned into a new simulator test so it can never silently regress.

**Scope:** the M4-specific real-store evidence — what the deterministic simulator structurally cannot show: that the abstractions DST simulates **match the real store**. Against the M4 single-zone topology under `tc netem` / `iptables` partitions / cgroup throttling / `libfaketime` clock skew:
- **Tier-1 integration** — end-to-end PUT/GET + multi-key atomic create/rename/delete on TiKV behind the unchanged trait; the bare composition swap and the direct M4 DoD / trait-leak retirement.
- **Tier-1 Jepsen** — a nemesis injecting real partitions, clock skew, and process pauses against the TiKV-backed cluster, validating the single-zone consistency clauses (linearizability of the commit point; exactly-one-winner under genuine concurrency). Extends the Jepsen line begun at M2 and extended at M3 across the backend swap; a clean public Jepsen result is a credibility artifact.
- **Tier-2** — a run on **one real machine** (real fsync, real NVMe, real OS) for honest single-node performance/I-O semantics (single failure domain → proves real-silicon behavior, not failure-domain independence).

Every behavior the real cluster surfaces that the redb fake did not model (txn-conflict timing, PD timestamp-oracle edge, a fault shape) is **promoted back into DST as a new seeded regression** wherever it manifests through the trait contract (ADR-0009; the FoundationDB/TigerBeetle pattern). **M4 must not re-prove atomicity against TiKV** — that is DST's job. Needs a real-TiKV-cluster fault seam in `testkit` and xtask runners (TiKV integration + Jepsen) wiring the `deploy/` compose into CI.

**Definition of done**
- [ ] Tier-1 integration + Jepsen consistency green in CI against real containerized TiKV under fault injection
- [ ] multi-key atomic create/rename/delete proven to hold under partition/contention
- [ ] at least one bug-finding discovery promoted to a **seeded DST regression** (seed committed)
- [ ] Tier-2 single-node real-I/O job green

**Needs:** M4.5 (deploy stack), M4.2/M4.3 (commit + scan). **Refs:** proposal 0007 §"DST and tests", §"Crate touch-points" (`testkit`, `xtask`), §"Suggested PR sequence" (6); ADR-0009, architecture §13.1/§13.4. Branch `feat/m4.6-tier1-jepsen-tier2`, commit `feat(testkit): … (M4.6, #<issue>)`.

comments.body: **Attached work from #259 (259.b — the mode benchmark):** the M4.6 Tier-1 campaign hosts `cargo xtask bench-meta` — four workloads (uncontended mix / hot-inode CAS storm / directory fan-in below 0015's scan paging cap / `NEXT_INODE_KEY` allocator storm) × both `TxnMode`s, measuring throughput, p50/p99, `Conflict` rate, and wasted retry work, **under `tc netem` RTT injection** (the modes are indistinguishable at localhost RTT; per 0015, Tier-2's single machine reports the latency floor but cannot discriminate). Static-endpoints topology per 0015 — not blocked on #365/#367. Decision rule + full plan: https://github.com/getwyrd/wyrd/issues/259#issuecomment-4871070333.

**Two attachments from the M4 open-question plans:** (1) from #262 — the Tier-1/Tier-2 campaign carries a **scan-envelope measurement leg**: bytes/entry for large-directory `scan` at realistic dirent counts *and* full-store `inode:` scan cost at realistic object counts (the custodian full-store scans are the real growth driver; numbers decide whether the paginated-scan trait evolution is ever filed). (2) from #263 — the Tier-2 sustained run's result is **logged into the #34 v1-stamping registry as evidence, not a stamping decision** (the go/no-go executes later at a forcing trigger; see https://github.com/getwyrd/wyrd/issues/263#issuecomment-4871179832).

milestone.title: M4 — Production metadata backend
milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: M4.6 — Tier-1 integration + Jepsen consistency over the backend swap; Tier-2 single-node real-I/O
